description: Derive the complete Multi Color Breathe report layout from immutable SteelSeries GG captures, including ordered colors and applicable zone or connected direction semantics, then add deterministic generation for earcup and supported microphone zones across profiles, CLI, and GTK.
design: Do not generalize the existing single-color Breathe builder until the additional coefficient records and color storage are proven. Use controlled captures for any ambiguous dimensions and require fixture equality before generated hardware writes.

notes:

title: Choose public project name and branding
description:
## Decision
Select the public repository, binary, application display name, and compatibility subtitle before GitHub publication. The decision is pending user acceptance; current recommendation is gamedacctl.

## Rationale
gamedacctl is immediately discoverable to Linux users, follows a familiar ctl naming convention, currently has no GitHub search collision, and appears less vendor-official than steelseries-gamedac-linux.

## Alternatives Considered
GlowDAC is a more neutral and polished brand but is less searchable and may be mistaken for an audio-DAC project. LumenDAC has the same ambiguity. Retaining steelseries-gamedac-linux is explicit locally but visually resembles a vendor-owned repository and is unnecessarily long for a binary name.
design: Prefer gamedacctl because it is discoverable, Unix-native, currently absent from GitHub search, and the ctl suffix reduces official-product ambiguity. Do not rename the local checkout or create a GitHub repository until the user accepts the name.
acceptance_criteria: Name is checked in the intended GitHub namespace, receives a basic package/web/trademark collision review, uses original artwork, and is documented with an independent-project compatibility disclaimer.
close_reason: Accepted gamedacctl for repository, package, binary, and future app; public namespace and crates.io collision checks passed; explicit unofficial compatibility disclaimer added; no artwork currently shipped.

title: Automate release publication with GitHub Actions
description: Replace the manually executed gamedacctl release process with a repository-owned GitHub Actions workflow. Resolve the current source-archive/PKGBUILD checksum cycle with a generated release recipe or checksum-substituted template. Grant contents:write only to the release job, never to pull_request code; pin third-party actions by commit SHA; do not expose signing credentials unless a separately reviewed signing design is adopted. Decide whether the Omarchy plugin needs its own lightweight tag/release workflow or only validation on controller releases.

title: Harden XDG profile storage
description: Audit and harden saved-profile persistence while preserving the existing $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gamedacctl/profiles.json location (default ~/.config/gamedacctl/profiles.json) and schema. The current location correctly follows XDG_CONFIG_HOME, but writes use a predictable .tmp name, permissions inherit the caller umask, the parent directory is not synced after rename, and concurrent GUI/CLI writers can overwrite newer state.
design: Keep lighting profiles and their user preferences in XDG_CONFIG_HOME because they are application configuration. Preserve version-1 files and the current path with no destructive migration. Use a unique temporary file in the same directory, restrictive user-only creation permissions, file sync followed by atomic rename and parent-directory sync, and a defined cross-process serialization strategy for GUI and CLI updates. A malformed store must produce an actionable error and must not be silently replaced. Package removal must leave user profiles untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Existing profiles load without migration or value changes; XDG_CONFIG_HOME overrides and the default ~/.config path are tested; new directories/files have intentional permissions; interrupted writes cannot replace the last valid store; concurrent CLI and GUI operations cannot silently lose profiles or the selected-profile state; malformed JSON remains recoverable and is never automatically overwritten; storage location, backup, and uninstall behavior are documented; full validation passes.
notes: 2026-09-05 implementation complete: preserved the version-1 XDG path and schema; all mutations now serialize through a private advisory lock and reload current disk state, then use a unique same-directory 0600 temporary file, file sync, atomic persist, and directory sync. The GUI no longer mutates its in-memory store before persistence succeeds and malformed initial data is surfaced without replacement. Added permissions, rejected-update, malformed-data, concurrent profile, concurrent selection/policy, default-path, and legacy coverage. Full scripts/validate passes with 23 library and 12 CLI tests. A read-only run against the owner actual four-profile store returned ready and preserved SHA-256 a4d4db2b35a5f28cd561f939c3508346304f32f609341176ba217bb72f80c0bd, mode 0644, and size 1035 exactly; its mode will become 0600 on the next successful write.

title: Derive reconnect readiness from passive HID input
description: Replace or shorten the conservative four-second reconnect delay only if unsolicited 64-byte input reports from GameDAC control interface 0 can be correlated with lighting-engine readiness. The HID descriptor exposes 64-byte input, 64-byte output, and 1024-byte feature reports; existing captures contain repeated device-to-host 0x10 reports and later 0x20 reports, but their semantics across enumeration are unknown.
design: Read unsolicited HID input passively through the known interface; do not invent a polling command. Keep the GUI responsive, bound all waits, retain a four-second fallback, distinguish kernel write completion from physical application, and verify audio recovery after each manual upstream reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: A labeled reconnect capture records enumeration, uaccess timing, first 64-byte HID input reports, attempted profile writes, and physical two-earcup results across repeated trials. A readiness predicate is implemented only if it predicts successful complete writes reliably; otherwise the tested fixed-delay fallback remains. No unknown output, feature, or firmware query is sent.
notes:
2026-09-05 preliminary passive trials: a settled three-second observation opened the control node but received zero 64-byte input reports. A complete 60-second manual upstream reconnect observation recorded input read failure at 19.392s, device absent at 19.647s, and /dev/hidraw15 accessible again at 35.176s; zero unsolicited input reports arrived before removal or after access returned. Existing capture 0x10/0x20 input records therefore are not a dependable heartbeat based on current evidence. Keep the physically accepted four-second post-access fallback; do not send an unobserved GET_REPORT or other query. A repeatable raw reconnect capture is still required before closing.

title: Select among multiple connected GameDACs
description:
## Problem
The controller currently selects the first matching 1038:1280 interface 0. That is convenient for the normal single-device case but ambiguous if more than one identical original GameDAC is connected.

## Scope
Enumerate matching compatible devices, preserve zero-configuration behavior when exactly one exists, and provide an explicit CLI/application selector when multiple matches exist. Refuse all writes while selection is ambiguous.
design: Use verified VID/PID/interface/report characteristics as the compatibility boundary. Prefer a device serial as the durable selector when exposed; otherwise present a clearly labeled physical/sysfs path with documented reconnect limitations. Never guess or silently choose the first device when multiple compatible units are present.
acceptance_criteria: One matching GameDAC continues to work without a selector; zero devices reports not found; multiple matches list distinguishable choices and fail closed until one is selected; tests cover enumeration and selection without hardware; the selected transport cannot open a different match; GUI/profile implications are documented.
notes: 2026-09-05 deferred after v0.1.3: the normal single-GameDAC path is safe and verified; selector work should resume when there is a real multi-device hardware/use case to validate identity and UX against.
